sources.policyExtinct: Extinct taxa: the last natural range before human-driven range loss or extinction, from late Pleistocene (c. 50-12 ka) to Holocene records. Post-contact relict ranges are not used as the whole range. Each rule's 'period' states the interval.
sources.africaSplits: Taxonomic splits mapped onto the parent species' PHYLACINE raster, restricted to the split taxon's regions.

elephantidae:mammuthusprimigenius.evidence: NPS Beringia mammoth-steppe account; broad historical envelope, current climate still required
elephantidae:mammuthusprimigenius.period: Late Pleistocene (c. 50-12 ka) mammoth steppe of Eurasia and Beringia

elephantidae:mammuthuscolumbi.evidence: NPS Waco/White Sands fossil records; broad continental envelope

elephantidae:mammuthusexilis.period: Late Pleistocene northern Channel Islands (Santa Rosae)

rhinocerotidae:coelodontaantiquitatis.evidence: NPS Beringia: woolly rhinos did not cross to Alaska

caninae:canislupastor.evidence: Koepfli et al. 2015, Current Biology 25(16): 2158-2165 (African golden wolf distinct from the Eurasian golden jackal; range Senegal-Morocco-Egypt to Kenya/Tanzania per https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_golden_wolf); PHYLACINE Canis aureus raster restricted to its African part
caninae:canislupastor.splitNote: Canis aureus sensu lato in PHYLACINE; only the African regions are used.

caninae:canislupusdingo.note: Introduced to Australia by people about 4,000 years ago (earliest confirmed remains c. 3,250 years old) and wild since; never reached Tasmania. Included as a long-established wild canid of mainland Australia.

caninae:cynotheriumsardous.period: Late Pleistocene-early Holocene Sardinia and Corsica

machairodontinae:smilodonfatalis.evidence: NPS Big Cats; broad historical envelope
machairodontinae:smilodonfatalis.period: Late Pleistocene North and western South America

pantherinae:pantheraatrox.evidence: NPS Big Cats; historical continental envelope

pantherinae:pantheraspelaea.evidence: NPS Beringia megafauna; Europe and northern Asia with Beringian North America

bovinae:bosprimigeniusprimigenius.note: European aurochs subspecies only; no automatic Indian/African aurochs substitution. Ireland excluded: no postglacial aurochs record there.
bovinae:bosprimigeniusprimigenius.period: Late Pleistocene-Holocene Europe and western Asia (last individual 1627, Poland)

sirenia:gigas.evidence: https://www.nhm.ac.uk/discover/stellers-sea-cow-first-historical-extinction-of-marine-mammal-at-human-hands.html; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steller%27s_sea_cow (Late Pleistocene Monterey Bay and Honshu, Amchitka); Crerar et al. 2014, Biology Letters (St Lawrence Island population c. 800-920 CE; bone provenance later questioned)
sirenia:gigas.note: Shallow North Pacific rim waters from Japan to California; the 1741 Commander Islands herd was a relict of this range.
sirenia:gigas.period: Late Pleistocene-Holocene North Pacific rim (relict to 1768)

iniidae:lipotesvexillifer.note: Middle and lower Yangtze main stem with Dongting and Poyang lakes; tributaries inside these boxes are not distinguishable. Functionally extinct since 2006.
iniidae:lipotesvexillifer.evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baiji (Yichang to the Yangtze mouth, Dongting and Poyang lakes, Qiantang River; declared functionally extinct 13 Dec 2006)
iniidae:lipotesvexillifer.period: 20th-century range (last natural range before its human-driven collapse)

manidae:mysteria.note: Cryptic pangolin described from seized scales; its wild native range is unknown.

capreolinae:pudellamephistophiles.evidence: North of the Huancabamba Depression after the 2024 split of Pudella carlae (Barrio, Gutierrez & D'Elia 2024, Journal of Mammalogy 105: 577-588)

capreolinae:cervalcesscotti.note: Broad eastern North American historical envelope; detailed fossil polygon pending.

thylacinidae:sarcophiluslaniarius.note: Late Pleistocene fossils from Naracoorte (SA), the Darling Downs (QLD), Western Australia and New South Wales.

casuariidae:bennetti.evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwarf_cassowary (montane and rain forests of New Guinea up to about 3,300 m); Folch et al., Birds of the World account (Cornell Lab of Ornithology)

casuariidae:unappendiculatus.evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_cassowary (lowland and swamp forest north of the Central Cordillera and west of Cendrawasih Bay, Yapen, Batanta, Salawati; usually below 490 m, recorded to 1,962 m)

casuariidae:tribonyxmortierii.note: Secure historical Tasmanian range; older mainland fossil range not yet enabled.

cervinae:megalocerosgiganteus.note: Broad historical Europe/Central Russia/Siberia envelope; present climate and open-habitat provider limits remain.
cervinae:megalocerosgiganteus.period: Late Pleistocene-early Holocene Europe to Siberia

meiolaniidae:ninjemysoweni.note: King's Creek, Darling Downs (Queensland); possible remains from New South Wales.

capreolinae:bretzianebrascensis.note: Pliocene-early Pleistocene deer outside the late Pleistocene-Holocene policy; no range.

capreolinae:odocoileuslucasi.note: Fossil deer without a documented late Pleistocene-Holocene range.

capreolinae:torontoceroshypnogeos.note: Known from a single antler (Toronto, c. 11 ka); one locality is not a range.

caninae:speothospacivorus.note: Known from the Lagoa Santa caves only; one locality is not a range.

bovinae:bubalusbrevicornis.note: Chinese Pleistocene buffalo without a documented range.

bovinae:bubaluscebuensis.evidence: Croft, Heaney, Flynn & Bautista 2006, Journal of Mammalogy 87: 1037-1051; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cebu_tamaraw

bovinae:bubalusmephistopheles.note: Neolithic and Bronze Age deposits across southern, central and eastern China, from Yunnan to northern Henan.
bovinae:bubalusmephistopheles.evidence: Yang, Liu, Chen & Speller 2008, Journal of Archaeological Science 35: 2778-2785 ("Wild or domesticated: DNA analysis of ancient water buffalo remains from north China"); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bubalus_mephistopheles
bovinae:bubalusmephistopheles.period: Holocene southern, central and eastern China (to c. 1200 BC)

bovinae:bubalusmurrensis.note: Interglacial European buffalo (last records c. 120 ka) outside the late Pleistocene-Holocene policy.

bovinae:syncerusantiquus.note: Scattered pan-African fossil record; no defensible late Pleistocene-Holocene range.

viverridae:genettaplesictoides.note: Endemic Cyprus genet of the Late Pleistocene (Aghia Napa).
viverridae:genettaplesictoides.evidence: Theodorou et al. 2007, Bulletin of the Geological Society of Greece 40: 201-208 (doi:10.12681/bgsg.16514); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetta_plesictoides

bovinae:bubalusgrovesi.note: Southern Sulawesi; the box covers the south-western peninsula (exact sites not verified).

vombatidae:vombatushacketti.note: South-western Western Australia (Mammoth Cave and nearby cave deposits).

caninae:dusicyonavus.note: Pampas and Patagonia; survived into the late Holocene.
caninae:dusicyonavus.evidence: Prevosti et al. 2015, Biological Journal of the Linnean Society 116: 704-720 (fossils from Argentina, Brazil, Chile and Uruguay); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dusicyon_avus
caninae:dusicyonavus.period: Late Pleistocene-late Holocene southern South America (to c. 700 BP in the Pampas, c. 400 BP in southern Patagonia)

elephantidae:loxodontacyclotis.evidence: Taxonomic split of the African elephant (forest elephant of the West and Central African rainforest belt); PHYLACINE Loxodonta africana present-natural raster restricted to that belt
elephantidae:loxodontacyclotis.splitNote: PHYLACINE lumps forest and savanna elephants.

bovinae:syncerusnanus.evidence: Forest buffalo of the West and Central African rainforest belt; PHYLACINE Syncerus caffer present-natural raster restricted to that belt

bovinae:tragelaphussylvaticus.evidence: Moodley & Bruford 2007, PLoS ONE ("Molecular biogeography: towards an integrated framework for conserving pan-African biodiversity"; scriptus lineage North and West Africa, sylvaticus East and southern Africa); PHYLACINE Tragelaphus scriptus raster restricted to East and southern Africa
bovinae:tragelaphussylvaticus.splitNote: Overlaps the provider's T. scriptus rule in East Africa; a 2023 morphological revision argues for a single bushbuck species.

caninae:canislycaon.evidence: Eastern wolf of the Great Lakes-St Lawrence region (Ontario, southern Quebec); PHYLACINE Canis lupus present-natural raster restricted to it
caninae:canislycaon.splitNote: Southern Ontario/Quebec only; north of 50 N remains gray wolf range.

capreolinae:mazamajucunda.evidence: Mantellatto, Gonzalez & Duarte 2021, Genetics and Molecular Biology (M. bororo Duarte 1996 is a junior synonym of M. jucunda Thomas 1913; restricted to the Atlantic Forest of Sao Paulo, Parana and Santa Catarina); PHYLACINE Mazama bororo raster

capreolinae:mazamarufa.evidence: Peres et al. 2021, Frontiers in Genetics 12: 742870 (Mazama rufa revalidated; fecal DNA shows it through the Atlantic Forest, Cerrado and southern Amazon); PHYLACINE Mazama americana raster restricted to those regions south of 4 S
capreolinae:mazamarufa.splitNote: Split from Mazama americana sensu lato.

capreolinae:odocoileuspandora.evidence: Gutierrez et al. 2017, ZooKeys 697: 87-131 (transferred pandora to Odocoileus); PHYLACINE Mazama pandora raster (Yucatan Peninsula)

capreolinae:pudellacarlae.evidence: Barrio, Gutierrez & D'Elia 2024, Journal of Mammalogy 105(3): 577-588 (southeast of the Huancabamba Depression, Peruvian yungas on the eastern Andean slope, 1,800-3,300 m); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pudella_carlae; PHYLACINE Pudu mephistophiles raster restricted accordingly
capreolinae:pudellacarlae.splitNote: Northern pudu (P. mephistophiles) is limited to north of the Huancabamba Depression.

vombatidae:zygomaturustrilobus.note: Widely distributed in Pleistocene Australia; this rule keeps the southern part, incl. Tasmania (Mowbray Swamp skeleton) and the Willandra Lakes (NSW).
vombatidae:zygomaturustrilobus.evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zygomaturus; Tasmanian Museum and Art Gallery skull TMAG Z3554, https://shapingtasmania.tmag.tas.gov.au/M/object.aspx?id=46
vombatidae:zygomaturustrilobus.period: Late Pleistocene southern Australia (extinct c. 45-33 ka)

capreolinae:antiferultra.note: Pampean region; genus-level fossil record from Argentina, Uruguay, southern Brazil and central Chile (species-level localities not verified).

capreolinae:rangifertarandusdomesticus.note: Domestic reindeer; no wild native range.

bovinae:bostaurustaurus.note: Domestic cattle; no wild native range (the wild ancestor is mapped as the aurochs).

bovinae:bubalusbubalis.note: Domestic water buffalo; no wild native range (the wild species is Bubalus arnee).

capreolinae:mazamatienhoveni.note: Described by van Roosmalen (2015) from the lower Rio Aripuanã basin; now usually treated as a synonym of Passalites nemorivagus, so the Amazonian brown brocket raster is used, limited to that basin.
